title: Radiosensitizing effect of a novel CTSS inhibitor by enhancing BRCA1 protein stability in triple-negative breast cancer cells.
authors: Choi, Eun; Jeon, Kyung-Hwa; Lee, Hanhee; Mun, Gil-Im; Kim, Jeong-Ahn; Shin, Jae-Ho; Kwon, Youngjoo; Na, Younghwa; Lee, Yun-Sil
one_liner_zh: 该文研究CTSS抑制剂通过稳定BRCA1蛋白增强三阴性乳腺癌放疗敏感性，属于肿瘤治疗与蛋白降解机制，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作或AI/物理模拟方法。
abstract: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) patients harboring wild-type breast cancer susceptibility gene 1 (BRCA1) account for most TNBC patients but lack adequate targeted therapeutic options. Although radiotherapy (RT) is the primary treatment modality for TNBC patients, radioresistance is one of the major challenges. RT-induced increase in cathepsin S (CTSS) causes radioresistance through suppressing BRCA1-mediated apoptosis of tumor cells, which was induced by CTSS-mediated degradation of BRCA1. Targeting CTSS may provide a novel therapeutic opportunity for TNBC patients. Publicly available data and human tissue microarray slides were analyzed to investigate the relationship between CTSS and BRCA1 in breast cancer patients. A CTSS enzyme assay and in silico docking analysis were conducted to identify a novel CTSS inhibitor. RO5461111 was used first to confirm the concept of targeting CTSS for radiosensitizing effects. The MDA-MB-231 TNBC cell line was used for in vitro and in vivo assays. Western blotting, promoter assay, cell death assay, clonogenic survival assay, and immunohistochemistry staining were conducted to evaluate novel CTSS inhibitors. CTSS inhibitors were further evaluated for their additional benefit of inhibiting cell migration. A novel CTSS inhibitor, TS-24, increased BRCA1 protein levels and showed radiosensitization in TNBC cells with wild-type BRCA1 and in vivo in a TNBC xenograft mouse model. These effects were attributed by BRCA1-mediated apoptosis facilitated by TS-24. Furthermore, TS-24 demonstrated the additional effect of inhibiting cell migration. Our study suggests that employing CTSS inhibitors for the functional restoration of BRCA1 to enhance RT-induced apoptosis may provide a novel therapeutic opportunity for TNBC patients harboring wild-type BRCA1.
abstract_zh: 携带野生型乳腺癌易感基因1（BRCA1）的三阴性乳腺癌（TNBC）患者占大多数TNBC患者，但缺乏充分的靶向治疗选择。尽管放疗（RT）是TNBC患者的主要治疗方式，但放射抗性是主要挑战之一。放疗诱导的组织蛋白酶S（CTSS）增加通过抑制BRCA1介导的肿瘤细胞凋亡导致放射抗性，这一过程由CTSS介导的BRCA1降解引起。靶向CTSS可能为TNBC患者提供新的治疗机会。本研究分析了公开数据和人类组织微阵列切片，以探讨乳腺癌患者中CTSS与BRCA1之间的关系。通过CTSS酶活性测定和计算机模拟对接分析，鉴定了一种新型CTSS抑制剂。首先使用RO5461111验证靶向CTSS以实现放射增敏效应的概念。采用MDA-MB-231 TNBC细胞系进行体外和体内实验。通过蛋白质印迹、启动子测定、细胞死亡测定、克隆形成存活测定和免疫组织化学染色评估新型CTSS抑制剂。进一步评估了CTSS抑制剂在抑制细胞迁移方面的额外益处。新型CTSS抑制剂TS-24增加了BRCA1蛋白水平，并在携带野生型BRCA1的TNBC细胞及TNBC异种移植小鼠模型中显示出放射增敏作用。这些效应归因于TS-24促进的BRCA1介导的凋亡。此外，TS-24还表现出抑制细胞迁移的额外作用。我们的研究表明，利用CTSS抑制剂恢复BRCA1功能以增强放疗诱导的凋亡，可能为携带野生型BRCA1的TNBC患者提供新的治疗机会。
